Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, [Operator Instructions]. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and Emily Carter, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights starting with our key strategic initiatives and the progress we've made. Before diving deeper into the financials with our CFO, Sarah Chen, I want to update you on these efforts and the concrete results. Our strategy is built on three core pillars: speeding up digital transformation, pursuing sustainable growth via varied revenue sources, and reinforcing our balance sheet to withstand economic volatility. We've pushed hard on these, achieving outcomes that set us apart from competitors even as the Fed normalizes rates and neobanks like Chime and Revolut ramp up pressure.

Digital transformation tops our list, now taking 65% of our tech budget, up from 52% last year. We've completed rollout of our advanced core banking platform, ApexOne, on a cloud-native setup with AWS and Temenos. This finished early for 85% of retail and commercial segments, cutting new feature launch times by 40% and trimming IT costs by $150 million a year via scalable operations. A key feature is our AI personalization tool, ApexAI Advisor, using machine learning on data from 28 million digital users. In Q3, it lifted cross-sell rates by 18%, like suggesting high-yield savings to checking customers, fueling a 12% year-over-year deposit rise to $245 billion.

For fraud, we've combined generative AI with behavioral biometrics, similar to JPMorgan's approach, dropping false positives by 35% and fraud losses to 4 basis points of volume from 12 last year. Mobile app daily users hit 4.2 million, up 22%, with Net Promoter Scores at 72 from 65. In the U.S., top-5 in digital deposits, Southeast growth was 15% from campaigns in Atlanta and Charlotte. Overseas, UK open banking under PSD3 added 250,000 API accounts with Plaid and TrueLayer, bringing $45 million in embedded finance fees.

Shifting to sustainable growth and diversification, we're emphasizing fees to protect our 3.45% net interest margin despite 25 basis point deposit beta from cuts. Wealth management at Apex Wealth Partners saw AUM up 14% to $420 billion, beating Morningstar peers, via ESG ETFs with BlackRock iShares—our Green Bond ETF grabbed $2.5 billion and 8% sustainable fixed income share. Payments shone: Visa Direct and Apex Pay gateway pushed volumes to $180 billion, up 28%, with $320 million fees, 19% higher year-over-year. Embedded finance via Apex Flex BNPL for Walmart and Target handles 1.2 million loans.

Asia-Pacific drives expansion post our $750 million buy of 51% in Singapore's NeoBank, reaching 5 million ASEAN customers, loan originations up 45% to SGD 3.2 billion at 4.1% NIM, NPLs managed at 1.8% with Basel IV IRB models. In Europe, Irish custody post-Brexit added €15 billion assets, aiding 13.2% CET1. Latin America JV with Nubank in Brazil originated $500 million micro-SME loans at 92% repayment, eyeing 20% ROE by 2026.

Our balance sheet pillar proved solid amid geopolitics and CRE softening. CRE portfolio down 22% to $45 billion, focused on multifamily/industrial under 65% LTV, provisions at 25 basis points—half peer median per S&P. Shareholder returns: $1.2 billion buybacks at $48 average, upping tangible book 8%, dividend to $0.62, up 10%. Tokenization pilot on Polygon for real estate securities targets $1 billion by year-end, potentially adding 50 basis points fees.

These align with our Digital First, Customer Centric focus, per McKinsey noting top banks get 55% revenue digitally. $2.8 billion tech spend past 18 months yields 3.2x ROI on $9 billion EBITDA add. AI ethics under EU AI Act and CFPB need watch, but acquisition costs down 17% to $145 per account, LTV up 24% to $4,200.

In short, we're leading: 11% core revenue growth, 15% EPS up, full-year guide 10-12% revenue, ROE over 14%. I'll now turn it over to Sarah for financial details.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $2.8 billion for the third quarter, or $2.10 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 10% driven by higher loan yields and robust deposit growth. Non-interest income was up 15%, reflecting strong performance in wealth management and trading activities. Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Let me expand on our fee income, which reached $2.5 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 28% of net revenues—our highest in five years. This shows our fee business holding up against inflation, Fed cuts signaling soft landing, and Europe geopolitics. Growth spanned wealth at 15%, investment banking at 8%, cards at 18%.

Wealth management delivered $1.125 billion, up 15%, 45% of fees. AUM rose 14% to $1.8 trillion on 8% organic net new money of $45 billion, beating Morgan Stanley and UBS, plus 6% market gains from S&P 12% YTD and APAC tech rebound. Fee rates up 20 bps to 62 bps via alternatives now 18% of AUM from 12%. Apex Prime robo-advisory drove 25% NNM from mass-affluent, costs down 30% with LinkedIn/app leads. North America 55% fees up 16%, EMEA flat 25% offset by Luxembourg, APAC 20% up 22% Singapore/HK. New Apex Legacy annuities got $10 billion commitments. Guide 12-15% FY24 fees assuming stable markets.

Investment banking $750 million, up 8% despite 5% M&A drop per Dealogic. Advisory $315 million up 12% on $120 billion deals like Eli Lilly $25 billion spin, TotalEnergies-Conoco. ECM $195 million up 25%, 4.2% US IPO share with Reddit/Rubrik; DCM $165 million steady at 450 bps HY. Mid-cap tech/industrials via IBX/Salesforce scored 15% conversions. US up 10%, Europe down 2% antitrust, APAC +18% China outbound. BlackRock Aladdin ESG bonds cut times 20%, $50 billion pipeline. $2.5 trillion backlog eyes 10% Q4 growth renewables/fintech.

Cards $625 million up 18%, fastest grower. Interchange/service $406 million up on 14% volume to $280 billion, spend/account $2,800 up 9% PCE 2.5%. Rewards 1.8% offset by Apex Black Visa Infinite 1.2 million adds. Merchant $140 million up 22%, Lightspeed 15,000 SMBs at 2.5% take. Wallets 55%, BNPL Apex Flex $40 million. US 60% +20%, LatAm 15% +25% Pix, EMEA 12%. $200 million Visa VDTP tokenization for 20% savings. Delinquencies 2.8% vs industry 3.2%, guide 15-20% FY24.

Fees' 12% rise shows balance, tech $1 billion FY24 boosts stickiness/margins for mid-teens 2025.

On capital returns, cornerstone of value: Q3 dividend $0.48/share up 6.7%, 13th straight growth, payout 38% in 35-45% target. Buybacks 42 million shares $2.1 billion at $50.25, YTD $3.8 billion vs $8 billion auth. CET1 12.1% Basel III standardized up 40 bps, 13.8% advanced, over 10.5% target and GSIB 2.5%. Excess $18 billion post CCAR where post-stress 9.8% beat by 400 bps over Wells/Citi.

Framework: earnings quality, regulatory resilience, growth flexibility. Post-2020 CET1 rebuild via 150 bps quarterly organic, RWA cuts 5% CRE ML models, blockchain collateral $4 billion RWA save by 2025. US middle C&I 15% share NIM 3.45% $2.5 billion excess. Europe EBA 11.2%, dividends for institutions. APAC 22% growth repurchases offset dilution Grab embedded.

2024 returns $12-14 billion: $3.2 billion dividends 7% DPS hike $1.98, $9-11 billion buybacks, 85-95% earnings, 4-5% share cut ROTCE 14-16%. 2025 $15 billion+ if CET1 >12.5% CCAR good. Basel III Endgame 10-15% RWA hit offset modeling; CRE $45 billion 4% loans 85% agency 250 bps cover; deposit beta 2.1% LDR 78%. Algo buybacks Citadel 70% off-exchange; supp div if CET1>13%; M&A tuck-ins 200 bps accretion.

Balance sheet moat enables returns while growing wealth 18%, payments Visa.

Next, provision for credit losses at $1.2 billion, up 15% QoQ 8% YoY, ACL $28.5 billion 1.45% loans up 5 bps, coverage 285% criticized. Driven by macro overlays, portfolio trends, CECL forward looks.

Macro: GDP 1.8% 2024, unemp 4.2%, adverse 20% prob unemp 5.5% CRE cap +100 bps, $450 million overlay up from $300 million office stress.

Portfolio: $1.97 trillion loans NCOs 45 bps up from 38 bps <55 avg. Delinq 1.12% up consumer: cards 2.8% vs 2.4% YoY revolving $1.1T, auto 1.1% subprime 20-30 bps underperform. CRE office $250 million special mention +15%, multi 0.8% NPL, C&I 25 bps. Mortgages 0.6%. US 75% 80% provision, Europe 15% IFRS9 1.4% NPL $150 million ECB pause, APAC 10% 1.0% $50 million ICBC JV.

Recoveries 25% gross CO, early delinq 1.8% +10 bps.

Methodology: CECL/IFRS9 5,000 pools FICO/LTV/DTI/geog/vintage. ECL=PDxLGDxEAD disc: PD logistic/ML 20+ macros +12% accuracy random forest; LGD 45% CRE office 25% mortgs -5 bps appraisals; EAD 40% draw stress. 3 scenarios Monte Carlo 1,000 sims, 2023 refresh Plaid/CoreLogic -18% uncertainty. Validation CRO, ECL committee, CCAR/DFAST 60 bps 2025.

De-risk CRE office -10% YoY $40 billion, subprime auto 15%; AI warnings 85% precision cards $200 million save. Next q $1.0-1.3 billion ACL 1.4-1.5%, CET1 12.2%.

Revenue diversification key in 5.25-5.50% rates: NII $4.2 billion +8% NIM 3.45%, non-interest 48% from 38%, loan demand soft.

Fees: wealth AUM $620 billion +22% $850 million +19% margins 32% Wealth360 AI leads -15% costs. GenAI ESG Aladdin 28% perf fees 60% sustainable $40T opp.

IB/mkts $1.1 billion +12% M&A -15%, ECM/DCM $45 billion #8 league.

Payments/treasury 2.5 billion txns +25% $720 million +30% ARPT $0.28 margins 65% 18% revenue PayHub Plaid/Stripe SMB pay-by-bank FX ERP 12% APAC.

Digital Neo 3.5 million users gamified 4.8% APY cross-sell 3.8 LTV $2,400 $450 million +45% interchange BNPL Shopify $200 million 12% yield <2% default ML.

Regions: NA 65% +18% CA tech +25% AUM; Europe 20% +35% SEPA UK +15%; APAC 12% +40% Grab/Sea 50 million RMB; EM 3% LatAm +60% Arg controls.

Non-interest 2.5x NII growth beta 0.2, ROTE 14.2% CET1 13.1%. Mitigate interchange caps derisk 80% recurring FX hedge 70%. FY24 $18-19 billion +16-20% 52% mix 2026, Q4 $10 billion green bonds Neo 5 million mid-teens EPS.

Credit quality resilient $450 billion loans high rates. Delinq 30-89 days 1.12% -5 bps seq -15 bps YoY third straight improve consumer. Auto 2.4% +10 bps <2.8% FDIC used car affor, cards 2.1% stable AI reminders +18% collections. C&I 0.8% -10 bps CRE 1.5% office focus.

NPL 0.92% -10 bps seq -25 bps YoY core 0.85% <Wells 1.05% JPM 0.98%. Mortg 0.6% -10 bps cure 65%, auto 1.2% LTV 105% dealer.

NCO 58 bps flat seq -65 bps YoY lowest 2 yrs. Consumer 1.85% cards 3.2% util -12% pricing, comm 15 bps CRE office $45 million. Recov 42% partners.

US 70% 0.88% NE/MW CRE 2.2% office 20% vac -40% new office multi/indust, Sunbelt <1% jobs. Intnl 1.1% Europe C&I 1.3% ECB UK mort 0.4% PRA.

GenAI FIS/Palantir early warn 45 days 22% less NPL. ACL 1.28% $5.8 billion 140% NPL 3.2x crit prov $420 million vintages +30% FICO +50 bps PD/LGD.

NCO low 50s YE 2% GDP unemp 4.5%, funding 60% dep CET1 11.5%.

I will now turn to David for risk.

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate especially office, consumer credit card and auto stress, and geopolitical impacts on trade finance. We are taking proactive steps like portfolio de-risking, AI early warnings, and stress testing to mitigate these and keep a strong profile.

Lisa Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loan ratio at 0.92% and net charge-offs at 58 basis points. Delinquencies at 1.12%. We've actively managed our loan portfolio, particularly commercial real estate where performance has been controlled through selective originations and sales. We remain confident navigating the economy.

Raj Singh:
Thank you. I'd like to update on technology initiatives. Significant progress in digital transformation, including ApexOne platform and ApexAI Advisor launch, which drove 22% mobile adoption increase, 18% cross-sell lift, and $150 million annual IT savings. Fraud AI cut losses sharply.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Focused on operational excellence: streamlining back-office via automation and supply chain partnerships, yielding productivity gains and $100 million cost savings this quarter.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jamie Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into revenue diversification efforts?

Michael Thompson:
Good morning, Jamie. As Sarah detailed, our push into fees, payments, and digital has non-interest at 48% of revenue, growing faster with lower rate beta. Impacts include 19% wealth fees, 30% payments, 45% digital streams, positioning for cycle-resilient growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Harris with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Harris:
What are your plans for capital returns going forward?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Tom. We're on track for $12-14 billion in 2024 via dividends up 7% to $1.98 DPS and $9-11 billion buybacks, 85-95% of earnings. Strong CET1 supports acceleration, with algo execution and opportunistic M&A tuck-ins, targeting top yields.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh:
How are you managing credit risk amid CRE and consumer pressures?

David Patel:
Priya, good question. Proactive de-risking CRE down 22% focused low LTV, consumer tightening subprime, ML models for PD/LGD. Provisions prudent, ACL coverage strong, stress tests clear hurdles comfortably.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks. Good morning, team. Could you walk us through the capital ratios, specifically CET1 and Tier 1—your current levels versus regulatory requirements? Any color on trends or regional nuances would be great.

Sarah Chen:
Good morning, Sarah. Happy to dive in. Our capital is rock-solid amid Basel III endgame. CET1 at 13.4% Q3 end, +40 bps QoQ from 13.0%, +110 bps YoY on 180 bps organic gen offset returns/RWA. Tier 1 15.2% with AT1 €1.5 billion 4.875% perpetual.

Regulatory: Pillar 1 CET1 4.5% Tier 1 6%, +2.5% cons buffer, 2.5% G-SIB like Morgan Stanley, Europe systemic 1.0%—total 10.5%, we're +290 bps over G-SIB median 12.8% EBA.

US 45% RWAs consumer/mkts CET1 13.4% eSLR 6.8%>5%, CCAR post-stress 10.2%>4.5% $4 billion buyback.

Europe Paris/Frankfurt €200 billion corp CRR3 RE floors CET1 12.9% IRB ECB -5% CRE RWAs.

APAC 20% RWAs Singapore/HK 14.1% trade PD/LGD China stable.

Trends: RoTE 11.5% €2.1 billion profits; RWAs +1.2% QoQ €650 billion opt shipping -15% auto sec; ML IFRS9 stage2 -200 bps €800 million CET1.

Inorganic €3 billion buybacks 10% div hike €0.85 45% payout.

Buffer for wealth $50 billion inflows low RWA, Basel IV floors offset 50 bps annual RWA cut.

Fortress capital, peer-leading, flexible growth.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Michael Thompson for any closing remarks.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Tech spend yields 3.2x ROI, 11% revenue growth.

Wealth: $1.125B +15%, AUM $1.8T +14% on organic NNM $45B, market gains, fee rates +20bps to 62bps, robo-advisory. IB: $750M +8%, advisory +12% on deals, ECM +25% IPO share, despite M&A drop. Cards: $625M +18%, volumes +14% to $280B, spend/account +9%, merchant +22%, BNPL.

Trends: organic +180bps, RWA mgmt.
